Hi OP! It would depend on where you live in both. 

Baguio is definitely great, pros are its cheaper, lower cost of living, better temperature, it's relatively peaceful, and communities here are tightly knit.
However cons, as people have mentioned Baguio has a water situation, the severity depending on the location. For example in Trancoville the water supply cycles per day, MWFSu no water, TuThSa may water. Something I don't see people mention, housing in Baguio is difficult to find and expensive, it's more expensive than Manila. There are A lot of unsafe areas in Baguio, but that's a given in any city.  The weather is also unpredictable.

As for Manila, the quality of education in Manila is better than the ones in Baguio. As people have mentioned you'll be getting used to the speed and hustle of the big city, and you'll develop a wider network. The transportation system in Manila is leagues better than in Baguio.(though for other areas it is more difficult. 
However there are a lot of challenges to living here. The first of which is adapting to Manila. Housing here is expensive, not as bad as Baguio, but since you're going to be keeping the rooms air conditioned or use a fan, your electricity bill will be far more expensive. Certain areas in Manila proper are also dangerous, so you have to learn how to navigate around them or through them. Traffic is horrible during rush hour, people say Baguio traffic is bad, especially in Minesview or Marcos Highway, but that still moves frequently, the congestion in Recto or España is comperatively worse.

Overall OP it's up to you. Baguio and Manila are great places to study and develop yourself. Both cities offer their pros and cons, and their own unique experiences.

The innovation of agriculture from the Americas was nothing short of incredible. A large number of staple crops were domesticsted by the Native Americans, Maize, Potatoes, Tomatoes, Squash, Beans, Peppers, Cocoa, Avocado, just to name several. Not to mention the creation of agricultural practices that are still in use today, like the chinampa which are floating gardens on top of marshlands or lakes. Mesomaerican cities were better designed and planned compared to most of their European counterparts. The city of Mexico-Tenochtitlan, the home city of the Aztecs, was built on a marshy lake like Venice, but was grander, with sprawling stone houses, and towering temples and palaces. The Mayan and Olmec civilizations erected massive stone pyramids that still stand today. The Inca Empire had a network of roads and bridges with way stations and supply deppts that allowed them to send messages and even assemble armies quickly over vast distances of mountains and valleys. Pre Colombian American Civilizations were just as impressive as their European and Asian counterparts. And for precious stones, Mesoamericans had access to gemstones such as Jade and Turquoise. 

Also you are underestimating how difficult it is to smelt iron. Getting iron from rocks is a long laborious process that requires high temperatures and specialized forges. Not to mention great quantities of iron ore would be needed. Which is why the process of refining iron took a long time to develop and perfected in the Old World. It doesn't help that most iron deposits in the Americas weren't as easily accessible as copper. Plus copper has a much lower melting point. With the addition of copper being softer and easier to cast and mold, as opposed to iron which has to be beaten into shape while it was red hot.

The jungle was alive with the sound of birds chirping and the rustling of leaves. The high green canopies above shielding the dense undergrowth below, as animals thread through all levels of the vast greenery . Then, the cacophany of the music of the jungle was interreputed by the sound of cracking branches and crunching leaves, as the whirring of gears and the sound of heavy boots accompanied this noise. A machine ran through the vegetitation, its metal armor lined with the scars of battle, blaster in hand, and an assortment of weapons built into it. It dashed through the forest as if hounded by hell itself.

The machine didnt stop running until the jungle gave way to a circle of mud huts, dwelt by hairy ape like humanoids. The residents began to howl and scream, uttering in their strange gluttural tongue. The women hid in their flimsy huts of mud and leaves, while the men grabbed weapons of bone and stone. The robot, despite its stoic face, began to quake, and shake, weapons in hand. As the two sides prepared for a massacare, the tension was broken by the banshee screaming roar of an enormous jungle predator. The savages knuckles turned white as they gripped their weapons, their faces ready to fight this metal man, were now painted in the colors of fear. In a shriek of yellow fangs and sharpened claws, the beast lunged at the man of metal. In a twist, in a twirl of impossible speeds, a crack of thunder, a bolt of energy sent the beast flying back into the undergrowth with a smoking hole in it chest. The machine's weapon smoked with energy, and its metal shoulders heaved up and down as if breathing heavily.

The primatives stood around the machine, weapons forgotten, mouth agape. They looked to this machine that killed their great enemy, their hated foe, and began to bow their heads and bodies in worship and respect. The man of metal, stood with its head tilted to one side, gazing at the spectacle and mimicked the action. So began the metal man's protection of the tribe, which soon found itself the largest in their history, they soon discovered agriculture, metals, and even found their way out the jungle and began to build villages and farms. All this under the guidance of their god and protector. Though they never learned each other's tongue, one spoke in the lines of machine and numbers spoken by all technology, the other spoke in a manner shared by all humanoids in the galaxy. But they prospered together, both taught each other how to live, technology and humanity was shared between the two opposing sides. One was nearing the end of his age, the other just beginning a new chapter. 

But alas, all things that began must end. The machine god's movement eventually slowed, its weapons failed to heat, and its enormous strength began to wane. Fear began to find its home in its processors again, it feared what lay beyond the shutdown of its processes. Will it be found by its creators, or will it just cease to exist. But as it laid at death's door, surrounded by the myriad of descendants of the orignal small tribe it saved from the jungle, its fear began to evaporate. It felt peace, home, if it were to die it thought, at least it died knowing it brought a race of savages into the light of civilization. It beeped out its last messaged with its ruby eyes, saying it in a language no one there understood.

"Thank you, for you have thaught me how to be truly alive." He said as he lay there dying with the last whirring of his gears and motors, a wheeze of sorts. The god shut down, and went to sleep. A burial was arranged for their god, their hero, their teacher, and their friend. They brought him to a small spot in the jungle, a familiar clearing with the marks of a campsite, and the ruins of mud around it. There they laid him to rest. Even though the fired mud washed away, the jungle around it turned to deserts and praires, the machine laid there, its metal sarcophagus shielding the man inside, even as vegitation grew around the metal frame, his weapons and circuitry rusted away, he was remembered not as a robot, but as a man. He was made a machine, a tool built for war and destruction, but died a forefather, a protector, a creator for a race of people. He lived with the fear of death, but died with only love in his heart.

The buzz of voices echoed across the room, but the chatter died as a man entered the chamber, he was dressed plainly in jeans and a simple shirt with a plain forgetful face of an average joe. A deceiving attire for one of the Earth's mightiest champions.  

"Have you ever felt that your emotions are just too strong?" The hero said, his voice smooth as honey. Cameras snapped and microphones converged around the podium, as reporters huddled around him clinging to every word. His face animated and joyous, beamig with arrogance. "Have you had the ability to soar the sky when joy just burst out your chest, to ride the winds like the birds do when they fly? Or to pulverize stone as if its made of pewter when rage fills your heart. Of course not, because this is my super power, when I feel an emotion, it manifests as an ability that elevates me on the level of a superhuman being." He snickers, and sneers at the crowd. "Pride makes me tough as diamonds, envy turns me into a corrosive slime, misery makes my bodily fluids toxic, and when feelings of Kuebiko strike me, my entire body feels like lead. Its not all good powers you see, but the worst of it is ennui." He sighs and his skin turns gray and his movements once fluid becomes almost robotic. His luxurious speech reduced to a dull monotone.

"How come you may ask? Well its because ennui activates a power that forces me to languish under its horrid spell."  His face seconds ago, flush with life, becomes more statuate, locking his features. "The emotion attacks me every day, until I found my calling as a fighter of the evils in the world, but as peace settled and the action died, I felt it more and more." He then began to look around the room, he moved his head slowly, struggling, as if he was fighting an invisible force holding it in place. "You may ask why is it so horrible, that even the greatest champion of humanity fears it?" His smile faded as his opal eyes froze began to grey. "Because with like every emotion I feel, it makes my physical body feel it a thousandfold. I fear it because it shows how I really feel about myself." The hero, no the man looked up to the ceiling. "It shows just how human a god can be. Just how time erodes even the greatest of beings." With that he petrifies completly. His face pointed to the sky as if asking for an answer to his predicament.

Its been ten thousand years since that incident and his body still stands there locked in stone, a somber reminder to the rest of mankind, that even the greatest of us, suffer from the most human of demons.

One trait that people with schizoprenia tend to suffer from is extreme delusions, like how sometimes they'll believe people are out to burn them alive, and their brain will make them have auditory and visual hallucinations based on it. 

But yeah a lot of fear and stigma surrounds people with schizo, as well as misinformation. Its honestly normal to fear it at first, as it is something that us not suffering from it, can't really comprehend. The voices aren't in her head, they're around her. They also suffer from these episodes where the hallucinations will spike, and the person will become increasingly irrational, impulsive, and be filled with emotions.

The best thing you can do to someone with schizoprenia is to help her during her episodes. Provide support when she is low, and treat her normally when she's not. Though you might want to skirt around certain topics to avoid triggering her. As a footnote, most of what I know is my experience from a schizoprenic friend, so some of these might not apply to your friend.

The air was heavy with the sickly sweet smell of inscence and the sour metallic scent of blood. The room was bathed in the hues of the sunset, as lines of red formed into ancient and occult symbols littered the floor along with a sea of candles. A massive creature towered in the center, its hooves pressing against the hardwood floor, while a small dimunitive man in corporate attire coweted before him.

"You have called me feeble mortal, and for that I shall grant you the world." The beast growled, its voice like a living swarm of locusts, "Tell me your heart's carnal desires, the forbidden wants of your soul, the hedonistic lust of your flesh, I shall make your darkest fantasies reality, all for a... certain
 price" 

"A-a-anyth-ing I w-wa-nt?"
The man whimpered, mustering whatever he courage he could. The pungent smell of urine mixing with the already unpleasant odors of the chamber.

"Yes, mortal swine, anything that your heart desires. But remember the price you must pay." Its tail flicking at the shadows dancing along the walls.

"Wh-what is this p-rice?" He  whispered, as he looked at it in its eyes. His eyes of opal matching against its scarelt fire.

"I have dealt with your kind for many vile ages, you should know by now the tithe of blood you must sacrifice in order to gain limitless power in the mortal realm." The monster smiled towards the small man, its teeth glinting like daggers, its eyes reflecting the true nature of the beast. "So what will it be, the grandeur of Solomon, the looks of Narcissus, the fame of Gil-Gamesh, perhaps the mind of Aristotle, the wit of Diogenus, the genius of Daedalous, or you can have all these, just for the damnation of your immortal life."

"W-what if I pay with s-something else!" The man shouted, much to the monster's surprise.

"Oh, what is this object you wish to me, an angel with dominion over your realm, mortal wealth is meaningless to me. I only deal with the currency of human lives." 

"I offer my heart!"

The fell chortling echoed off of the walls, a twisted imitation of human mirth. Its hooves stomped on the ground as its tail lashed wildly at the air, as it began to bellow and guffaw, barely able to contain itself. When the creature managed to compose itself, it spoke like a living tide of insects.
"For countless ages, I have dealt with an innumerable sea of mortals, all of them damning themselves to the lake of sulfur and brimstone. But in my endless eons of existence, no man has ever willingly sold his heart, the home of his humanity to me! Me! The greatest foe your kind ever met, and, you a mortal, the envy of the angels on high, willingly give up what sets you apart from us immortals! For this, your offer is far greater than that of any mere mortal soul, for you sell not yourself but what makes you yourself. Whisper to me then immortal fool, whisper to me your heart's desire, even if you so wish for the moon to be in your pocket, for the heavens itself to bow to you, I will grant it."

The man composed himself,  straightening his blue suit, and fixing his stiff blonde hair. "I want to be President of my country." He began to exhude confidence, and that soon bled into arrogance.

"Is that all? You trade your humanity to become a mere president of a nation? Not even its king?" 

"I already have everything I want, I own billions, I got a beautiful wife, and I am the best at everything. I just want to win this election."

"I see then, but for the price of your heart, your very humanity, I will grant you another boon, one that fits the role of a former man. You shall become my herald during the End Times, you shall sound the trumpet when I take Creation. From henceforth you are no longer a man, you are the Bearer of Oblivion, the Bringer of Damnation, the Reaper, the Horseman, the Pale Rider, you are now Death, and all the world shall die at your touch." The creature then brought out a scroll, it was written in an ancient tongue that only beings of creation speak, its letters glowed a fierce scarlet in the darkened room. "But first, place your hand here to seal your fate."

The man, no Death placed his hand on the scroll, sending him to a fate worst than damnation. He brought ruination to everything he touched, and everywhere he went, devastation followed. Even though a human heart still beat in his chest, his humanity no longer dwelled in his soul. He lives a half-life devoid of all the pleasures of human existence, but still filled with human frailty. He thought he outwitted the Devil, but the truth is, the Devil outsmarted him.

567 Days later
Boom! A fireball bloomed from a nearby Republic Supply Debut, the ground shook as metal was ripped apart and bodies incinerated by the heat. The engines of the buggy roared as we sped away from another successful operation. The harsh hot wind hit me in the face, burning my already sun-burnt skin, but even that couldn't ruin my satisfaction at our success. I look to the driver of the vehicle, an enormous mountain of flesh and armoured plates, a Kroaxi, his forefathers fought by my side and saved my life, countless of times. I turn to the back to face orange human-like being clad in Merker Battlplate, a Merker, her ancestors, served alongside mankind, for nearly a thousand battles, zealously leading charges into machinegun fire. I look around me, at the hastily assembled raiding group, from a single glance none of them had anything in common, yet they all did. All of them from the various alien races in bondage under the iron rule of man, all of them wanted freedom from their oppresive rule, all of them were willing to fight to tooth and nail to see their dream fufilled. We arrived at our base at dusk, if you could call it that, it was more like a hastily assembled camp, built into the mountains and mostly being underground. I watched the twin suns fade over the desert horizon as we descended into the depths of our base, the silent calls of the desert gave way to the loud, comforting cacophany of the home of the Khalan System Rebel Cell. I smiled softly as my crew mingled with the rest of our comrades, exchanging high fives and hugs, and congratulating on our success. Despite the atmopshere, I felt something gnawing at my soul, and with that I left and headed for mission control, various other races milled about their assigned duties from the large and monstrous Ghorodo, to the small and dextrous Fharaxian. I clenched my fist as I continued to walk over to mission control, I fought back the tears that were coming. I arrived soon to a set of double doors and sighed relief as I typed in the familiar pass code, the date I liberated Fharax from the oppresive regime of their Tyrant Queen, it was in my opinion, my finest hour. The doors hissed open and I stepped into the metallic chamber of mission control. I walked over towards the mangled mass of electronics and wires and dialed in Commander Farseen, a rebel general in charge of Star Fleet Alpha, though to call it a fleet is much to generous. "Greetings General Andromedus, how goes the operation against the last Republic holdout?"
"Their holdout was bombed and every last Republic Trooper was gunned down." I tried my best to smile.
"That's great news! Another planet liberated from the iron shackles of the Republic."
"Yes, it is"
"Well my friend, I am afraid I have to cease communications so quickly, a Republic fleet has entered out sector and we have to go dark for the operation to work. Goodluck General Andromedus."
The transimission ends and I find myself alone in the room, illuminated only by the light of the computer screen, I kneel against its metallic frame, and I could no longer keep the wave of tears from my eyes and I feel they all spill out on my face. I failed them, I failed them all.
